learning_objective: 🎯 Experience the touching nostalgia of a child! Understand how memories of a lost loved one stay alive through everyday sights, sounds, and smells.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: The poet (Rabindranath Tagore) lost his mother when he was very young. He openly admits that he cannot remember her face or physical features clearly.
Even without a face, he feels his mother's presence. When he plays with his toys, he feels a tune 'hovering' over them—the very tune his mother used to hum while rocking his cradle.

During autumn, the sweet scent of Shiuli flowers fills the morning air. Because his mother used these flowers for temple prayers, their scent brings back an overwhelming feeling of his mother's presence.
When he looks up at the distant blue sky, he feels as if his mother's loving, protective gaze has spread all over the sky, watching over him from above.

fun_activity.title: 🌬️ The Smell of Memory
fun_activity.instructions: Close your eyes and think of a smell that reminds you of a specific person or place (like the smell of rain, your grandmother's cooking, or a specific soap). Scents are the strongest triggers for memories!

exam_tips: 📌 This deeply emotional poem is written by Rabindranath Tagore.
📌 Identify the three sensory triggers that remind the poet of his mother: Sound (the lullaby tune), Smell (Shiuli flowers), and Sight/Feeling (the vast blue sky).
📌 Explain how the poem shows that a mother's love is eternal and transcends physical death.
quick_recap: ⭐ The poet cannot remember his mother's physical face, but he vividly feels her essence.
⭐ Shiuli flowers are associated with the autumn season and morning temple prayers.
⭐ The vast blue sky symbolizes the mother's limitless, all-encompassing love and protection.
